Rarity.maps_to: Potion.rarity = 'uncommon' (potions.py:213), read by shop.MerchantPotionEntry pricing and by potion_pools.POTION_POOL's rarity bucket (potion_pools.py:38-65)
Rarity.rationale: EXECUTED, not asserted: `py audit/tools/potion_probes.py sweep-attrs` extracts PotionRarity from every C# model and diffs it against the sim class attribute over all 51 units and reports 0 mismatches. Rarity is observable in the sim (it sets the shop price and the reward-roll bucket), so this is a behavioural verdict rather than a field copy.

Usage.maps_to: no explicit attribute; the sim's only potion-use entry point is CombatState.use_potion (combat.py:583-616), which cannot be reached outside a combat
Usage.rationale: PotionUsage.CombatOnly means the game's Use button is live only during a fight. The sim reaches that by construction: `py audit/tools/potion_probes.py sweep-usage` finds exactly one `def use_potion` in sts2_rl/, on CombatState, and the conformance driver only dispatches the recording's UsePotion command inside a live fight (conformance/combat_driver.py:16,263-289). The absence of a `usage` attribute is therefore not a dropped guard for this unit -- but it IS a real gap for the four AnyTime potions, which is where the divergence is filed (blood_potion, entropic_brew, foul_potion, fruit_juice).

TargetType.maps_to: no attribute -- `targeted` stays False, so CombatState.use_potion passes target=None (combat.py:608) and the potion applies to ctx.player (potions.py:216-229)
TargetType.rationale: TargetType.Self in a single-player run always resolves to the owner: PotionModel.EnqueueManualUse defaults `target` to `Owner.Creature` when it is a valid target (PotionModel.cs:240-243) and IsValidTarget's Self/AnyPlayer arms accept exactly that creature (PotionModel.cs:280-287). The multiplayer half -- AnyPlayer letting you throw the potion at an ally, and CanThrowAtAlly (PotionModel.cs:381-388) gating it on `RunState.Players.Count > 1` -- is out of scope by the shared contract and noted in maps_to rather than verdicted as a divergence.

OnUse (protected override, GamblersBrew..issue: Rollup of guard G1 per binding rule 4. The verbs and the count match -- select from hand with MinSelect 0, then `CardCmd.DiscardAndDraw(list, list.Count)` (GamblersBrew.cs:27) vs discard each pick and `DrawCmd.draw(player, len(chosen))` (potions.py:224-229) -- and the hook ORDER inside DiscardAndDraw matches too (N1). What diverges is that the sim cannot express a partial pick, so the brew always cycles the whole hand.

guards.what: G1 (LIVE): MinSelect 0 -- the game lets you pick ANY NUMBER of cards including none; the sim always takes every candidate
guards.issue: MECHANISM (shared with potion/ashwater, the only other MinSelect-0 potion; one mechanism, two sites). The prefs are `new CardSelectorPrefs(SelectionScreenPrompt, 0, 999999999)`, and FromHand's auto-resolve shortcut `!prefs.RequireManualConfirmation && list.Count <= prefs.MinSelect` (CardSelectCmd.cs:708-711) is false for any non-empty hand with MinSelect 0 -- so the screen is ALWAYS shown and the player may confirm 0, 1 or all of it. CombatState.select_cards has no minimum/maximum pair at all: it clamps `count = min(count, len(candidates))` and returns exactly that many (combat.py:575-581), and both installed selectors return the full count -- selectors.scripted_card_selector, the env default (full_env.py:788), returns `keyed[:count]` (selectors.py:83), and the engine fallback is `self._rng.sample(candidates, count)` (combat.py:581). LIVE: the potion is a pooled Uncommon (potion_pools.py:52) and the divergence is a whole hand's worth of cards, which the RL observation encoder reads directly. The mechanism IS expressible in the sim -- selectors.py:79-82's 'gambling_chip' branch filters the candidates instead of taking `count` -- so this is a missing minimum/maximum on select_cards, not a missing capability. The conformance replay is unaffected (conformance/combat_driver.py:74-111 reads the recorded SelectHandCards picks), so grade B rather than a stream desync.

guards.what: N1: DiscardAndDraw's per-card hook order, and what it actually defers -- the C# doc comment overstates it
guards.rationale: SETTLED AGAINST THE BODY, not the comment. CardCmd.cs:162-167's summary says DiscardAndDraw 'will wait to trigger the discard-related hooks until after the draw is complete', which would make the sim's per-card `hooks.on_card_discarded` before the draw (potions.py:226) a gap. The BODY does not do that: CardCmd.cs:186-195 fires `Hook.AfterCardDiscarded` inside the per-card loop, BEFORE the `CardPileCmd.Draw` at :199. The only thing genuinely deferred past the draw is the Sly auto-play (:201-204). So the sim's ordering is right and the port's own docstring (potions.py:208-210) is right; a batch that trusted the C# summary would have filed a false gap. See N2 for Sly and N3 for the within-card ordering.

guards.what: N2 (dormant): the Sly auto-play deferral has no sim counterpart
guards.issue: CardCmd.cs:184-204 collects every discarded card with `IsSlyThisTurn`, and after the draw auto-plays each of them with AutoPlayType.SlyDiscard. The sim has no Sly concept at all: `grep -rn '\bsly\b' sts2_rl/` returns exactly one hit, the docstring at potions.py:210 that names it. DORMANT because no ported card or power grants Sly, so the slyCards list would always be empty. What would make it live: porting any card with the Sly keyword, at which point discarding it to Gambler's Brew should play it for free after the draw and would instead do nothing. Filed as a dormant gap rather than waived, per binding rule 1 -- 'no ported content triggers this' is not a waiver.

guards.what: N3 (dormant): the sim fires on_card_discarded BEFORE the card reaches the discard pile; C# fires it after
guards.issue: C# per card: `CardPileCmd.Add(card, discardPile)` then `History.CardDiscarded` then `Hook.AfterCardDiscarded` (CardCmd.cs:192-194) -- the card is already in the pile when the hook runs. potions.py:225-227: `player.hand.remove(card)`, `ctx.hooks.on_card_discarded(card)`, then `player.discard_pile.append(card)` -- the hook runs while the card is in NEITHER pile. DORMANT, executed: `grep -rn 'def on_card_discarded' sts2_rl/` finds only the dispatcher (hooks.py:409) and no listener at all, so nothing can observe the difference today. What would make it live: any ported listener on on_card_discarded that reads the discard pile or the card's pile -- a discard-counting relic reading `len(discard_pile)` would be off by one for the duration of the dispatch.

guards.what: W: the shared PotionModel.OnUseWrapper pipeline every potion resolves through (audit/content/potion/shared-mechanisms.md)
guards.issue: MECHANISM, shared by all 51 units and recorded once per record because PotionModel is one of harness.py's MODEL_ROOT_CLASSES, so no unit record enumerates it -- and unlike CardModel/PowerModel/RelicModel it is NOT covered by any seam record either, which is the coverage hole audit/content/potion/shared-mechanisms.md exists to name. src/Core/Models/PotionModel.cs:291-342 in order: :293 RemoveBeforeUse (sim combat.py:603-606 nulls the slot and detaches the listener before the effect -- faithful); :297 Hook.BeforePotionUsed; :327 OnUse (this record's own hooks); :336 CombatManager.History.PotionUsed (no sim entry -- PotionUsedEntry.cs:9-38 adds only a Description string and an executed grep of src/ finds no game reader, so presentation only); :338 Hook.AfterPotionUsed (sim hooks.py:566-571 on_potion_used, dispatched at combat.py:610 -- faithful); :340 CheckForEmptyHand. TWO of those are LIVE gaps, and both are already owned by another record, so this entry MATCHES their verdicts per binding rule 3 rather than re-deriving them. (1) BeforePotionUsed has no sim dispatcher at all -- hooks.py declares only on_potion_used, whose own docstring says it mirrors AfterPotionUsed -- and its single C# implementer SurroundedPower.cs:82 is ported at powers.py:2523, so throwing a potion at the far Kaiser Crab arm does not turn the player to face it: audit/records/power/surrounded.json, gap, live. (2) CombatManager.cs:887-893 CheckForEmptyHand has exactly two callers, CardModel.cs:1992 and PotionModel.cs:340, and the sim's only on_hand_emptied call site is player.py:197 -- the end-of-turn flush CombatManager.cs:880-883 explicitly excludes: audit/records/relic/unceasing_top.json G1, gap, LIVE, executed with a potion witness. Reachable from EVERY potion, not only the hand-emptying ones, because C# tests the hand AFTER the use. Rollup `gap` per binding rule 4.

guards.what: W4: PotionModel.cs:324-331 brackets OnUse in BeginCardOrPotionEffect/EndCardOrPotionEffect and the sim has no re-entrancy depth counter
guards.issue: CombatManager.cs:889's `!IsExecutingCardOrPotionEffect(player)` is what stops a nested effect from triggering the empty-hand check early, and PotionModel.cs:324-331 is what puts a potion inside that bracket. The sim has no counterpart anywhere. DORMANT for the same reason audit/records/relic/unceasing_top.json G2 is dormant -- the ported cards that auto-play another card mid-resolution (cards/cascade.py:58, cards/colorless_skills.py:117) do not touch the draw pile between the inner and outer ends -- but recorded separately because the OUTER frame here is a potion, so a fix that brackets only card plays would leave this half open. What would make it live: any ported potion or card that empties the hand and then moves the draw pile from inside a nested auto-play.
